briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 22, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Emergency: Failure of the 1.5-Degree Target and Deepening Threats
sections.content: Criticism is mounting that the goal of limiting the global average temperature increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius has virtually failed, with a perceived lack of will to defend it [2]. A UN report stated that limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius is no longer feasible, warning that warming will almost double if countries do not change course [69, 75]. Specifically, the UN report identified the United States as one of the major causes of the global retreat in climate change response [67, 83]. Reports indicate that climate change is costing California billions of dollars, and there is a growing possibility of immense financial burdens on the state's taxpayers [65, 82]. Thus, the international community's failure to achieve climate goals and the resulting economic and social ripple effects are becoming increasingly evident.

sections.title: ⚠️ Extreme Climate Phenomena: Changing Disaster Paradigms and Warnings
sections.content: Climate change is altering the patterns of natural disasters globally, including heatwaves and heavy snowfall [7]. Extreme weather events, such as Himalayan floods and heatwaves on the Korean Peninsula, are occurring frequently, interpreted as warnings of the climate crisis sent by glaciers [8]. In Colorado, a record 'water year' was observed as 'absurdly warm,' raising concerns that climate change is disrupting Western weather [60, 66]. Direct impacts of climate change, such as rock avalanches hitting Arctic glaciers, are appearing in various locations [63]. These changes are increasing the need for developing climate change-resistant crop varieties in the agricultural sector [5]. Furthermore, discussions on migration changes amidst the current climate crisis are underway [6], suggesting the importance of continuously observing and analyzing signals from nature, much like the ocean's records that interpret climate change [1].

sections.title: 🌱 Acceleration of Domestic Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: A seismic shift is occurring in the domestic power mix, as renewable energy installed capacity has surpassed coal power generation capacity for the first time, now accounting for 25.4% of total power generation facilities [32, 35, 36, 37, 39, 40, 42, 45]. This supports the forecast that renewable energy will become the largest power source in Korea within 2-3 years. International cooperation is also active, with the Korea Energy Agency dispatching a 2026 Renewable Energy Vietnam Trade Delegation [33, 40]. However, despite plans for 87 GW of solar power generation facilities, concerns are being raised about a potential reversal in renewable energy policy, due to a shortage of ESS (Energy Storage Systems) – the 'vessels' for electricity – and wavering incentives for public participation [48, 55]. Furthermore, while measures are being sought to improve resident support and siting procedures for power grid construction and expand renewable energy profit sharing [34], there is also a critical perspective that clean energy alone cannot solve climate change [74].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Efforts and Policy Recommendations for Achieving Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Diverse domestic and international efforts are continuing to address climate change and achieve carbon neutrality. Samsung Electro-Mechanics has actively responded to climate change through sustainable management and received a Presidential Commendation for its contributions to promoting eco-friendly technologies [3, 49]. Discussions are also underway to deepen the Green Partnership between Korea and the European Union (EU) [4]. Domestically, the Namyangju Carbon Neutrality Support Center has opened, Ulsan Metropolitan Office of Education is strengthening climate crisis response education [11, 14], and various local governments such as Gwangmyeong City and Changwon City, along with businesses and civil society organizations, are actively conducting carbon neutrality campaigns and events [16, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 27, 28, 31]. Internationally, China has surpassed 1 billion tons in cumulative carbon emissions trading volume, making significant progress in climate action [86, 90], and the world's first task force to protect communities from climate change has been established in the UK [84, 91]. However, challenges remain, such as criticisms that the LNG power generation for the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster runs counter to carbon neutrality goals [13, 23], and that climate targets are threatened by the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the UK North Sea [10, 92].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has simultaneously highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, positive signals in the transition to renewable energy, and diverse efforts towards carbon neutrality. This is a time that calls for continued attention and action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
